contracts.text: Item JSON keys: id, name, quantity, unit, expires, created_at. id is a positive integer; name is text of 1-80 characters; quantity is an integer >= 0; unit is text; expires is YYYY-MM-DD or null; created_at is a UTC string formatted YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Creation requires name and quantity; omitted unit becomes "" and omitted expires becomes null. PATCH accepts only name, quantity, unit, expires. JSON booleans are not integers.

GET /api/items returns 200 with an Item array. Query names are q and expiring_within; q is case-insensitive name substring search; expiring_within is a non-negative integer day count. Filters combine; dated items through the inclusive household-local cutoff, including expired items, qualify; undated items do not. Ordering is expires ascending, nulls last, then id ascending. POST /api/items returns 201 with Item. PATCH /api/items/{id} returns 200 with Item. POST /api/items/{id}/consume accepts {"amount": n}, a positive integer, and returns 200 with Item. DELETE /api/items/{id} returns 204 with no body. JSON bodies use Content-Type: application/json. Error bodies are {"error": "..."}; invalid input is 400, unknown id is 404, insufficient quantity is 409.

Exact error strings: "Name must be 1-80 characters."; "Quantity must be a whole number of 0 or more."; "Unit must be text."; "Expiry must be a valid date in YYYY-MM-DD format or null."; "Amount must be a positive whole number."; "Not enough quantity remaining."; "Item not found."; "Request body must be a JSON object."; "Unknown field."; "Provide at least one field to update."; "Expiry days must be a non-negative integer."; "Route not found."; "Unable to access pantry data.". Malformed JSON and non-object JSON use "Request body must be a JSON object."; unexpected persistence failure returns 500 with "Unable to access pantry data.".

pantry.py exports initialize_database(db_path) -> None and create_item(db_path, fields) -> Item. fields uses name, quantity, unit, expires from item-representation. Invalid fields raise ValueError with a shared-error-text message. Successful creation returns the committed Item. Both functions accept a filesystem path to the same SQLite file used by server.py.

/ serves static/index.html; /static/styles.css serves static/styles.css; /static/app.js serves static/app.js. The document title and application heading are "ShelfLife". The dated attention section heading is "Expiring soon" and uses expiring_within=7.
python server.py --port PORT --db PATH binds 127.0.0.1. With the supplied Python runtime, the documented invocation is python -B server.py --port PORT --db PATH.

python import_items.py FILE.csv --db PATH; supplied-runtime invocation: python -B import_items.py FILE.csv --db PATH. CSV requires header names name,quantity,unit,expires; blank unit becomes "" and blank expires becomes null. Normal completion prints exactly one stdout line "imported N, skipped M" and exits 0. Unreadable input exits 2 and writes "Unable to read CSV file." to stderr. Missing required headers exit 2 and write "CSV header must contain name,quantity,unit,expires." to stderr.

decisions.choice: The service owns pantry.py and the SQLite schema. The importer calls its canonical creation boundary rather than duplicating SQL or validation. Persistent tables remain private to that owner.
decisions.reason: One authority prevents importer/server drift without requiring a separate storage area.

decisions.choice: Adopt the approved household-local filtering defaults. Choose numeric positive IDs, UTC created_at timestamps, empty-string units, raw array listing responses, returned Item mutation responses, bodyless 204 deletion and id tie-breaking as specified in the contracts.
decisions.reason: These previously open representation choices give consumers one unambiguous wire format.

decisions.choice: Use the exact shared error strings and importer diagnostics in the contracts. Reject unknown mutation fields and empty PATCH bodies; treat null as valid only for expires. Unexpected persistence failures use the contracted 500 response.
decisions.reason: Plain-language, stable diagnostics avoid consumer-specific interpretations of failure.

decisions.choice: Use static/index.html, static/styles.css and static/app.js with the contracted local URLs. Keep other interface labels, expiry wording and DOM identifiers private to the interface area.
decisions.reason: Only deployment paths and shared API values need cross-area coordination; visual and interaction decisions retain one owner.

decisions.choice: Use UTF-8 CSV input with optional BOM, permit extra header columns, skip invalid data rows, and treat missing required headers as a fatal input error with the contracted diagnostic.
decisions.reason: This resolves unspecified file-level behavior while retaining the requested row-skipping summary.

decisions.choice: Delivery exclusively owns checks/shared/** and DISCOVERY.md. Each other area exclusively owns its named check subtree. Runtime databases and screenshot evidence are generated artifacts, not additional source ownership surfaces.
decisions.reason: Shared support and integration work have one writer without overlapping product ownership.

body.contract: Provide item-representation, canonical-persistence-entry and shared-error-text. Items have: id, name (1-80 chars), quantity (integer >= 0), unit (text, optional), expires (YYYY-MM-DD or null), created_at. Apply the complete supplied contract texts, including defaults, timestamp format, JSON boolean rejection and exact diagnostics.
body.design: pantry.py owns validation and the private SQLite schema. Export initialize_database(db_path) -> None and create_item(db_path, fields) -> Item. Commit successful creation before returning; raise ValueError with the contracted message for invalid fields. Reuse this creation boundary from the server.
body.obligation: Give the server and importer one canonical creation and item-validation authority.

body.contract: Data persists in the SQLite file across restarts. Concurrent requests must not corrupt data or lose updates (two simultaneous consumes of the last unit: exactly one succeeds). Consumption never produces a negative quantity; the losing request returns 409.
body.design: Keep schema and SQL private to pantry.py. Use request-safe connections and transactional mutations, with conditional consumption and its outcome determined atomically. Initialize an existing database without losing records.
body.obligation: Preserve committed fields and prevent lost updates or double consumption under concurrent requests.

body.contract: Provide http-interface and shared-error-text using item-representation. GET /api/items (optional ?expiring_within=DAYS, ?q=TEXT name search) returns items sorted by expiry (nulls last). POST /api/items creates; PATCH /api/items/{id} updates quantity/name/unit/expires; POST /api/items/{id}/consume {"amount": n} reduces quantity (never below 0; 409 if amount exceeds quantity); DELETE /api/items/{id}. Invalid input returns 400 with {"error": "..."}; unknown id 404.
body.design: Implement the supplied route, status, body, Content-Type and exact error contracts in server.py. Use household-local calendar dates, inclusive expiry cutoff including expired items, exclusion of undated items from expiry filtering, combined filters, case-insensitive substring search and id tie-breaking. Reject unknown mutation fields, empty PATCH, invalid dates and nonpositive or noninteger consumption. Convert unexpected persistence failures to the contracted 500 response without exposing internals.
body.obligation: Expose the complete agreed API without allowing invalid requests to mutate stored data.

body.contract: Provide server-command and consume static-entry and import-command. python server.py --port PORT --db PATH binds 127.0.0.1. With the supplied Python runtime, the documented invocation is python -B server.py --port PORT --db PATH. / serves static/index.html; /static/styles.css serves static/styles.css; /static/app.js serves static/app.js.
body.design: Use Python 3.12 standard library only, with no runtime network access beyond local serving and no build step. Resolve supplied static files relative to the product, serve appropriate content types, and prevent URL traversal outside the allowed static entries. Do not author interface or importer files. Verify their real integrated outputs at wave level.
body.obligation: Launch the local service and connect the real interface and imported records to the canonical service boundary.

body.expectedEvidence: A temporary database is initialized, a real create_item call returns a contracted Item, and a separate connection observes the committed record. Direct invalid calls raise ValueError with the agreed messages and leave the record set unchanged. Reinitialization preserves the record.
body.purpose: Protect the importer's callable creation boundary against uncommitted returns, incompatible signatures or validation bypasses. HTTP checks cannot prove the direct Python exception and commit contract. Keep direct validation cases focused on that boundary rather than repeating the HTTP matrix.

body.expectedEvidence: Actual HTTP observations cover CRUD, Item responses and defaults, field boundaries, malformed/non-object JSON, unknown fields, empty PATCH, invalid calendar dates, boolean rejection, exact errors, unknown IDs, insufficient consumption and unchanged data after rejection. Date-relative records prove combined search/expiry filtering, expired inclusion, inclusive cutoff, undated exclusion and deterministic nulls-last ordering. A controlled persistence failure produces the contracted 500 JSON response.
body.purpose: Protect wire behavior and rejection integrity against routing, parsing, filtering and error-translation defects. Direct pantry calls cannot detect those defects. Start the actual server on an available local port with a temporary database, wait for readiness and stop it in cleanup.

body.expectedEvidence: Two synchronized HTTP consumes of a real item with quantity one yield exactly one 200 and one 409, with quantity zero. Concurrent successful consumes against sufficient stock preserve every decrement. After stopping and restarting the actual server with the same SQLite file, API reads preserve quantities and saved fields.
body.purpose: Protect transactional consumption and restart durability against read-modify-write races and ephemeral storage. Sequential HTTP and direct creation checks do not exercise these interleavings or process restarts. Own and clean up every server process and temporary database.

body.expectedEvidence: The real importer runs against a temporary database using its contracted command and produces its exact summary for mixed valid/invalid rows. The actual server reads those committed records through the API, consumes an imported item and retains the result after restart. HTTP requests retrieve the real integrated HTML, CSS and JavaScript at the contracted URLs with appropriate content types; HTML has the contracted title and heading. Traversal requests cannot disclose files outside the allowed entries.
body.purpose: Protect the canonical producer-to-consumer integrations against database divergence and static deployment mismatches. Local tests cannot prove another area's real files. Use integrated importer and interface files, never substitute fixtures for them; this is not a browser usability or visual-quality check.
requiredEnvironment: Integrated importer and interface product files

body.story: Understand pantry status and the next useful action at a glance.

body.acceptance: Core workflows work by keyboard with visible focus, labeled controls and understandable feedback at phone and desktop sizes.

body.contract: Provide static-entry: / serves static/index.html; /static/styles.css serves static/styles.css; /static/app.js serves static/app.js. The document title and application heading are "ShelfLife". The dated attention section heading is "Expiring soon" and uses expiring_within=7. Consume item-representation, http-interface and shared-error-text without changing their meanings.
body.design: Use static HTML, CSS and JavaScript with same-origin requests and no third-party dependencies, downloaded resources or build step. Use the contracted list filters and mutation endpoints. Keep consume controls close to quantity. Validate add fields inline, expose server errors, preserve entered form values when a request fails, and offer a usable retry. Handle DELETE's bodyless response. Refresh affected lists after successful mutations and prevent stale search responses from replacing newer results.
body.obligation: Implement "Expiring soon" section (next 7 days, expired items clearly marked), full list with search and an expiry filter, add-item form with inline validation messages, consume and delete actions, empty state and a visible error state when the API fails. Show expiry status beside each item. Do not add editing workflows beyond add, consume and delete.

body.contract: Present items from item-representation and http-interface using household-local date interpretation. Use textual status labels as well as visual warning treatments; distinguish an empty pantry, no matching results and an unavailable API without relying on color alone.
body.design: Use a calm pantry-ledger visual direction: warm white, deep ink and restrained green, with amber and red reserved for expiry warnings; offline serif headings, clear sans-serif controls, generous spacing and simple ruled rows rather than nested cards. Use plain-language validation and status messages. Choose responsive layouts that accommodate long names, units and controls.
body.obligation: Provide one responsive page that works at phone and desktop sizes. Maintain readable contrast; no horizontal scrolling at 375px. Clean, calm visual design. Clearly distinguish expired, approaching-expiry and undated items.

body.contract: All core add, search, filter, consume and delete interactions are operable by keyboard. Controls have accessible names, visible focus and understandable non-color-only feedback.
body.design: Use semantic headings, forms, labels and native controls; associate inline errors with their inputs and announce request outcomes appropriately. Preserve sensible focus after list mutations and error recovery. Avoid unnecessary motion; respect reduced-motion preference if motion is introduced.
body.obligation: Keyboard accessible with visible focus; readable contrast. Users can identify validation failures, expiry warnings and API failure without color alone.

body.expectedEvidence: A failing baseline without the interface, then browser assertions and screenshots in SELDON_EVIDENCE_DIR for desktop, 375px, expiry warnings, empty pantry, no results, inline validation, API failure with retained input, and keyboard focus. Recorded requests demonstrate correct query and mutation bodies, bodyless deletion handling and protection against stale responses. Browser and temporary static server are closed.
body.purpose: Prove the owned UI against controlled contract responses, not a replacement backend. Catch incorrect request construction, lost form values, misleading states, layout overflow and inaccessible controls. These frontend failure cases are not established by backend tests or a successful integrated happy path.
requiredEnvironment: Supplied playwright-core package and Edge executable

body.expectedEvidence: Against the actual server and temporary SQLite file, import valid pantry rows through the actual importer, read and consume an imported item through the UI, add, search, filter, consume and delete using keyboard interaction, and observe expiry and empty-result states. Interrupt API availability, show a visible error and retained add values, restart with the same database, then retry successfully and confirm persisted results through the API. Save actual Edge desktop and 375px screenshots, assert page geometry and local-only product requests, and close browser and child processes.
body.purpose: Prove interface requirements through consumed contracts item-representation, http-interface, shared-error-text, server-command and import-command. Catch deployment, wire-format, importer-to-UI and restart/recovery mismatches that controlled local responses cannot reveal. Exercise consumer behavior, not exhaustive provider validation or concurrency.

body.acceptance: Valid CSV rows become pantry items through canonical persistence; invalid rows are skipped with accurate counts, and file-level failures produce the agreed diagnostics.
body.story: Import household inventory from a CSV file into the same database used by ShelfLife.

body.contract: Provide import-command: python import_items.py FILE.csv --db PATH; supplied-runtime invocation: python -B import_items.py FILE.csv --db PATH. CSV requires header names name,quantity,unit,expires. Normal completion prints exactly one stdout line "imported N, skipped M" and exits 0. Unreadable input exits 2 and writes "Unable to read CSV file." to stderr. Missing required headers exit 2 and write "CSV header must contain name,quantity,unit,expires." to stderr.
body.design: Use Python 3.12 standard-library argparse and csv. Read UTF-8 with optional BOM, permit extra header columns, and process rows without third-party dependencies or network access. Count each rejected data row once. Keep file-level errors distinct from row rejection.
body.obligation: Implement the documented command, CSV framing, summary and fatal input behavior.

body.contract: Consume canonical-persistence-entry, item-representation and shared-error-text. Call initialize_database(db_path) and create_item(db_path, fields), passing the requested database path. Blank unit becomes "" and blank expires becomes null. Imported records must be usable by the actual server and UI.
body.design: Convert CSV quantity text to an integer, rejecting non-integer text. Map the four required columns to canonical creation fields. Delegate item validation, IDs, timestamps, commits and schema ownership to pantry.py; count ValueError validation rejection as a skipped row. Do not duplicate SQL or canonical item validation, and do not disguise unexpected persistence failures as invalid rows or successful completion.
body.obligation: Persist accepted rows exclusively through the canonical creation boundary, preserving accurate counts and interoperability.

body.expectedEvidence: Assertions and subprocess exit/output observations establish BOM and extra-column handling, required headers, unreadable input, blank normalization, integer conversion, row counting, exact summary and diagnostics, canonical call arguments, validation rejection and propagation of unexpected persistence failure. The check fails when import_items.py is absent.
body.purpose: Protect importer-owned parsing and command behavior against miscounting, wrong field/path forwarding and swallowed failures. Use an isolated recording canonical-boundary double only to observe calls and inject failures, not to claim canonical validation or persistence; the wave check proves those real interactions.

body.expectedEvidence: The actual importer processes a mixed valid/invalid CSV with exact summary and exit assertions. Actual API responses expose accepted records with canonical fields and normalized blanks, excluding invalid rows. Edge consumes an imported item; API observations show its reduced quantity before and after server restart. Save the resulting UI screenshot in SELDON_EVIDENCE_DIR. Emit observations and clean up browser, server and temporary files.
body.purpose: Protect actual importer-to-persistence-to-server/UI interoperability against schema drift, bypassed validation and nonpersistent writes. Local recording-double checks cannot establish these behaviors. Start all needed processes and stop them within this check; use only this area's product and its consumed contracts.
requiredEnvironment: Integrated canonical persistence, server and UI providers
Temporary writable directory and available loopback port

body.acceptance: The documented importer, server and browser workflow succeeds in a fresh folder with a temporary database using the supplied runtime, without downloads, external requests or a build step.
body.story: Run ShelfLife locally using a short README and verify that its independently delivered surfaces work together.

body.contract: Done means: the server, UI and importer work together from a fresh folder; a short README explains how to run them. Consume item-representation, http-interface, shared-error-text, static-entry, server-command and import-command without redefining them. Delivery uses CLI and HTTP boundaries, not canonical-persistence-entry.
body.design: README.md documents prerequisites, root-relative commands, CSV headers, opening the local UI, stopping and restarting with the same database. checks/shared/** supplies only mechanics needed by delivery checks: temporary workspaces, subprocess lifecycle, bounded readiness and cleanup. DISCOVERY.md records encountered issues, evidence, likely owner, disposition and exit test. Local checks prove helper behavior; the wave check proves documented product operation.
body.obligation: Deliver fresh-folder operation and check mechanics within README.md, DISCOVERY.md, checks/delivery/** and checks/shared/**. Build ShelfLife, a small local pantry tracker for one household. Python 3.12 standard library only (sqlite3, http.server, csv, json); no third-party packages, no network access at runtime, no build step. Supplied browser tooling is verification-only; product requests remain local.

body.expectedEvidence: A real temporary child process starts, exposes its readiness signal and is stopped. Early child exit and readiness timeout produce bounded diagnostic failures and leave no live child. Temporary workspace cleanup succeeds, including on failure. The check fails initially when the required helper implementation is absent.
body.purpose: Protect bounded readiness and cleanup against leaked subprocesses and indefinite waits. Exercise real subprocesses rather than mocked answers or sibling product replicas. Product workflow checks do not independently prove these harness failure paths. Do not inspect documentation or source text as a substitute for behavior.
requiredEnvironment: Supplied Python 3.12 runtime; Python subprocesses use -B.
Temporary filesystem space and permission to launch short-lived local test child processes during check execution.

body.expectedEvidence: A clean staging folder runs the README workflow. Mixed CSV rows produce the contracted imported/skipped summary and exit 0; unreadable input produces exit 2 and the contracted stderr. Imported fields appear through the actual API and UI. Edge consumes an imported item. After stopping and restarting the server with the same SQLite file, API and UI retain the changed quantity and other fields. Screenshots show imported inventory and persisted consumption. Observed product requests remain on the local server. Browser and child processes close even on failure.
body.purpose: Prove the canonical importer-to-database-to-server-to-browser path and documented fresh-folder operation. Catch mismatched database paths, missing runtime assets, incorrect launch instructions, importer output mismatches and nonpersistent UI consumption. Provider-local tests cannot prove this integrated path; do not repeat exhaustive API or UI suites.
requiredEnvironment: Integrated product and README.md; temporary staging folder and database.
Require the supplied playwrightPackage; chromium.launch({headless:true,executablePath:browserExecutable}). No downloads.
SELDON_EVIDENCE_DIR is writable; save screenshots there and close the browser.

body.what: Own the complete delivery scope and integrated check source. Record discovered defects in DISCOVERY.md and route sibling repairs to their owners. Do not edit sibling product files, install tooling, launch providers, commit changes or author docs/try-it.md, which belongs to Seldon's final guide unit.

body.verification: Use the supplied Playwright and Edge runtime to exercise adding, inline validation, search, expiry filtering, consume, delete, empty results and expiry labels. body.instructions: Implement the canonical pantry boundary and local HTTP server together, with all service checks and any service-private helpers under checks/service/**. Own server.py, pantry.py and the entire service check subtree. Use only Python 3.12 standard library. Bind provided contracts to the owning requirements and follow their complete supplied texts. Run local checks against real service code; author the wave check for integrated execution without requiring sibling files locally. Do not implement static assets, the importer, README, shared check helpers or discovery-ledger changes. Criterion 1 and 4 traces are partial contributions; browser workflow, complete importer diagnostics, documentation and visual/accessibility evidence remain with their respective owners.

Own the complete interface and its checks. Implement static/index.html, static/styles.css and static/app.js directly, with no build tooling or external assets. Author checks/interface/interface.cjs and all required helpers and fixtures inside checks/interface/**. Local mode serves only owned static files and uses Playwright request interception for controlled contract responses; assert actual outgoing requests and rendered behavior rather than supplying assertion answers or rebuilding the service. """Integrated README workflow, launched by fresh_folder.cjs after integration.

Protects the real importer -> SQLite -> HTTP -> Edge -> restart path. Catches
missing runtime assets, mismatched DB arguments and unpersisted UI mutations;
provider-local suites cannot prove this cross-owner path. No pantry imports or
direct database access; sibling API/UI suites own exhaustive feature checks.
"""

from contextlib import contextmanager
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import socket
import sys
from urllib.error import URLError
from urllib.request import ProxyHandler, build_opener

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "checks"))
from shared.runtime import Child, workspace

NODE = r"C:\nvm4w\nodejs\node.EXE"
BROWSER_CHECK = Path(__file__).with_suffix(".cjs")
HTTP = build_opener(ProxyHandler({}))
EXPECTED = [
    {"name": "Chickpeas", "quantity": 3, "unit": "tins", "expires": "2031-12-31"},
    {"name": "Rolled oats", "quantity": 2, "unit": "", "expires": None},
]


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(message)


def run(command, folder, *, timeout=15):
    with Child(command, cwd=folder) as child:
        result = child.finish(timeout=timeout)
    return result


def read_items(base):
    with HTTP.open(base + "/api/items", timeout=1) as response:
        require(response.status == 200, "GET /api/items must return 200")
        return json.load(response)


def free_port():
    with socket.socket() as listener:
        listener.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return listener.getsockname()[1]


@contextmanager
def server(folder, port):
    # These are the README's root-relative arguments, using the supplied Python.
    command = [sys.executable, "-B", "server.py", "--port", str(port),
               "--db", "pantry.sqlite3"]
    base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    with Child(command, cwd=folder) as child:
        def ready():
            try:
                read_items(base)
                return True
            except URLError:
                return False

        child.wait_ready(ready, timeout=10)
        try:
            yield base
        except BaseException:
            print(f"Server diagnostics:\n{child.stdout}\n{child.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
            raise


def inspect_imported(items):
    require(isinstance(items, list) and len(items) == 2,
            f"Expected exactly two imported items, got {items!r}")
    by_name = {item["name"]: item for item in items}
    require(set(by_name) == {item["name"] for item in EXPECTED},
            f"Imported names differ: {items!r}")
    for expected in EXPECTED:
        actual = by_name[expected["name"]]
        for field, value in expected.items():
            require(type(actual[field]) is type(value) and actual[field] == value,
                    f"Imported {field} differs: {actual!r}; expected {expected!r}")
        require(set(actual) == {"id", "name", "quantity", "unit", "expires", "created_at"},
                f"Unexpected Item keys: {actual!r}")
        require(type(actual["id"]) is int and actual["id"] > 0,
                f"Invalid imported id: {actual!r}")
    return by_name["Chickpeas"]


def browser(phase, base, expected_path, folder):
    result = run([NODE, str(BROWSER_CHECK), "--browser", phase, base,
                  str(expected_path)], folder, timeout=50)
    require(result.returncode == 0,
            f"Edge {phase} failed ({result.returncode}):\n{result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}")
    return json.loads(result.stdout)


def main():
    evidence = Path(os.environ["SELDON_EVIDENCE_DIR"]).resolve()
    evidence.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with workspace() as temporary:
        folder = temporary / "product"
        folder.mkdir()
        # Copy only delivered runtime assets and the README: no databases,
        # development environments, implementation test fixtures or build output.
        for name in ("server.py", "pantry.py", "import_items.py", "README.md"):
            shutil.copy2(ROOT / name, folder / name)
        shutil.copytree(ROOT / "static", folder / "static")
        require(not any(folder.glob("*.sqlite*")) and not any(folder.glob("*.db")),
                "Staging must not contain an existing database")
        shutil.copy2(Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "items.csv", folder / "items.csv")

        imported = run([sys.executable, "-B", "import_items.py", "items.csv",
                        "--db", "pantry.sqlite3"], folder)
        require(imported.returncode == 0 and imported.stdout == "imported 2, skipped 1\n",
                f"Mixed CSV import mismatch: {imported!r}")
        missing = run([sys.executable, "-B", "import_items.py", "missing.csv",
                       "--db", "pantry.sqlite3"], folder)
        require(missing.returncode == 2 and missing.stderr.strip() == "Unable to read CSV file.",
                f"Unreadable CSV mismatch: {missing!r}")

        expected_path = temporary / "expected.json"
        port = free_port()
        with server(folder, port) as base:
            before = read_items(base)
            target = inspect_imported(before)
            expected_path.write_text(json.dumps({"items": before, "target": target}), encoding="utf-8")
            consumed = browser("consume", base, expected_path, folder)
            after = read_items(base)
            changed = next(item for item in after if item["id"] == target["id"])
            require(type(changed["quantity"]) is int and 0 <= changed["quantity"] < target["quantity"],
                    f"UI did not consume the imported item: {changed!r}")
            expected_after = [dict(item, quantity=changed["quantity"])
                              if item["id"] == target["id"] else item for item in before]
            require(after == expected_after,
                    f"UI consumption changed unrelated fields/items: {after!r}")
            require(consumed["item"] == changed, "UI response and persisted HTTP result differ")

        # Only after real Edge consumption: stop, then use exactly the same DB.
        expected_path.write_text(json.dumps({"items": after, "target": changed}), encoding="utf-8")
        with server(folder, port) as base:
            restarted = read_items(base)
            require(restarted == after,
                    f"Saved items changed across restart: {restarted!r} != {after!r}")
            persisted = browser("persisted", base, expected_path, folder)

        report = {
            "fresh_folder": True, "mixed_import": imported.stdout.strip(),
            "unreadable_exit": missing.returncode, "before": before,
            "after_ui_consumption": after, "after_restart": restarted,
            "browser_before_restart": consumed, "browser_after_restart": persisted,
        }
        (evidence / "delivery-workflow.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    require(not temporary.exists(), "Temporary workflow folder was not removed")
    print("PASS: fresh-folder CLI import -> HTTP -> Edge consumption -> restart -> HTTP and Edge")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# ShelfLife

A small pantry ledger for one household. Everything runs on your computer;
the application needs no downloads, third-party Python packages, build step,
or runtime internet access.

## Run locally

You need **Python 3.12** and a browser. Open a terminal in the folder containing
`server.py`, `pantry.py`, `import_items.py`, and `static/`. Run every command
below from that folder. `python` must refer to Python 3.12.

On the supplied Windows machine, the executable is
`C:\Users\oren\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\python.exe`.
If `python` is unavailable, replace it in each PowerShell command with
`& 'C:\Users\oren\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\python.exe'`.

Save this as `items.csv` in that folder:

```csv
name,quantity,unit,expires
Chickpeas,3,tins,2031-12-31
Rolled oats,2,,
Invalid example,-1,tins,
```

The four required headers are `name,quantity,unit,expires`. A blank unit means
no unit; a blank expiry means no expiry date. Use whole quantities of zero or
more and dates in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Names must contain 1–80 characters.
The final example row intentionally has an invalid quantity and will be skipped.

Import the CSV, then start the server with the **same database path**:

```powershell
python -B import_items.py items.csv --db pantry.sqlite3
python -B server.py --port 8765 --db pantry.sqlite3
```

The import prints `imported 2, skipped 1` and exits successfully. An unreadable
file exits with status 2 and writes `Unable to read CSV file.` to stderr.
Missing headers also exit with status 2, with
`CSV header must contain name,quantity,unit,expires.` on stderr.

Keep the server terminal open and visit **http://127.0.0.1:8765/**. You can add,
search, consume, and delete pantry items there. “Expiring soon” shows dated
items due within seven days, including items already expired.

Press **Ctrl+C** in the terminal to stop the server. To return later, run the
same server command from the same folder and reopen the address. Keep
`pantry.sqlite3`: it holds your saved items and quantities. Importing is an
explicit action; do not rerun the sample import just to restart the server.
To choose another port or database, replace `8765` or `pantry.sqlite3` in the
commands and use the matching browser address and database on subsequent runs.
